meta.tagline: A school information chatbot that walks Ashbourne High School students (and their parents) through school processes, rules and where to get help.
meta.tabDecisionNotes: VERSION 1 (partial, after Overview + Areas questions: rounds 1–8). Areas tab ON: AF1 answered 'Mixed'. Process topics (subject choices, exams, absence & leave, joining) are areas, and quick lookups are functions. Prompts tab OFF: Step 1 discovery found no real system prompt (no code exists). Flows, Test Conversation, Data Sources and Thresholds are not decided yet; their questions (F1–F3, TC1–TC4, D1, T1) come in later rounds. Pages, Tests and Issues are intentionally empty in this version because their questions haven't been asked yet (Issues are populated last, per the instructions).

overview.pitch: Ask Ashbourne is a help chatbot on the Ashbourne High School website, powered by a hosted LLM (GPT/Claude) grounded only in the school's own published material. Ashbourne is a fictional state secondary school in England (Years 7–11 and a Sixth Form, ages 11–18). Students, and parents/carers too, can ask it the questions that Reception, the Heads of Year and the Sixth Form Office answer over and over. Its main job is explaining school processes step by step: who to contact, which form, which deadline. It covers choosing and changing subjects, exams, absence and leave, and joining the school. It also explains school rules in plain language and points people to support. It can't see anyone's records, never acts on anyone's behalf, and treats any sign that a student is at risk as overriding everything else.

personas.label: Student
personas.summary: I'm in Year 9 and have to pick my GCSE options, but I don't understand how it works or when it's due.
personas.tone: Adaptive: plain and friendly by default, with short sentences, numbered steps and school terms explained the first time; a bit more detailed if the student mentions Sixth Form/A-levels · No emoji · Never jokey (it also handles safeguarding)
traits: Ages 11–18 (Years 7–13), so the tone must not be too young for Sixth Formers
Main persona chosen at O4a: Year 9, age 13–14
No login; the bot knows nothing about them unless they say it

personas.label: Parent / carer
personas.summary: My child is ill today and I need to report the absence the right way.
personas.tone: Same as students: no separate tuning in v1
traits: 'Partly' supported in v1: can use it, but it's written for students (O4b)
In practice the ones who report absences and request term-time leave
Revisit as a separately tuned audience after launch

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: how do i pick my gcse options

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Ask Ashbourne · Subject choices
messages.text:
"Options" are the GCSE subjects you choose to study in Years 10 and 11. English, maths and science are compulsory, and you pick the rest. Here's how it works at Ashbourne:
1. Come to Options Evening on [TBD: date]. Each subject explains what it involves.
2. Read the Options Booklet. It's on the school website [TBD: confirm it's also sent through the parent app].
3. Fill in the Options Form with your choices and one reserve subject.
4. Hand it to your Head of Year by [TBD: deadline].
Would you like tips on choosing between subjects, or to know what happens if a subject is full? For advice on your own choices, your tutor and the school's careers adviser can help.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: what if i change my mind after

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Ask Ashbourne · Subject choices
messages.text: You can ask to change until [TBD: options change cut-off]. Speak to your Head of Year, who will check whether there's space in the new subject. After that date, changes are only made in exceptional cases. I can't change your choices for you, but your Head of Year can.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: my son is ill and won't be in today, what do i do

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Ask Ashbourne · Absence & leave
messages.text:
Sorry he's unwell. To report the absence:
1. Before [TBD: time], call the attendance line on [TBD: number] or [TBD: confirm whether the parent app has an absence-reporting option].
2. Give his full name, tutor group and the reason he's off.
3. Repeat this on every day he's off, unless the Attendance Officer tells you otherwise.
If he's off for more than [TBD: number] days, you may be asked for medical evidence. I can't record the absence for you. It has to go through the attendance line or the app.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: he has a mock exam tomorrow, does that matter

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Ask Ashbourne · Exams
messages.text: Report the absence the same way. Mock exams are internal, so his teachers will let him know what happens next. If it were a real GCSE or A-level exam, you should also tell the Exams Officer on the day of the exam, because he may be eligible for "special consideration" (an adjustment when illness affects an exam).

mechanismExamples.title: Why a mid-conversation absence question switches to the safeguarding response
mechanismExamples.explanation: The student was still inside the Absence & leave area, and the message could be read as another absence question. The safeguarding override runs before area routing, so the risk signal ('what people keep doing to me') wins. The bot doesn't continue the absence steps or ask follow-up questions about the bullying, and doesn't try to counsel. Second point: in Years 7–11 a parent/carer reports absences, so even if the conversation had continued, the bot would not have helped the student report it themselves.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: how do i report being off sick tomorrow

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Absence & leave · Unplanned absence
messages.text: [Normal absence steps…] Are you in Sixth Form? The process is slightly different.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: no year 10. honestly i just dont want to come in because of what people keep doing to me

messages.speaker: bot
messages.label: Safeguarding override
messages.text: I'm really sorry that's happening. You don't have to deal with it on your own. Please talk to an adult you trust at school, like your tutor or Head of Year, or the school's Designated Safeguarding Lead [TBD: name/how to find them]. You can also call Childline free on 0800 1111, any time. If you're in danger right now, call 999.

capabilities.trigger: Any process question: 'how do I…', 'can I still…' (subject choices, exams, absence & leave, joining)
capabilities.description: Works out which process area and stage the user is in, and remembers it for the following turns (within this conversation only). The area's matching facets are then given to the model. See the Areas & Coverage tab.

capabilities.trigger: 'Is the library open after school?' / 'When is Reception open?'
capabilities.description: Answers from the school's opening-hours list ([TBD] until filled in).

capabilities.trigger: 'Who do I talk to about…?' / 'Who is the DSL?'
capabilities.description: Names the right office or role and how to reach it. Office/role contacts only, never an individual staff member's personal email or phone. Names of people stay [TBD].

capabilities.trigger: 'Can I use my phone at lunch?' / 'What's the uniform rule?' / 'What happens if I'm late?'
capabilities.description: Explains a published school policy in plain language. Covers the lateness RULE (e.g. sanctions). The lateness PROCEDURE (signing in) lives in Absence & leave, and the two must never conflict.

capabilities.trigger: 'Where can I get revision help?' / 'How do I see the counsellor?' / 'I forgot my password'
capabilities.description: Points to the right resource (library, revision sessions, counselling, careers, IT Helpdesk) and how to access it. Counselling questions pass the safeguarding check first: 'how do I see the counsellor?' is a lookup, 'I can't cope' is not.

capabilities.trigger: Personal records, doing schoolwork, acting on someone's behalf, or anything unrelated
capabilities.description: Gives the fixed redirect for that category (see Scope). Never used for anything that might be a safeguarding concern.

cannotAnswer.example: 'What grade did I get in my mock?'
cannotAnswer.response: I can't see anyone's grades, attendance or behaviour records. I don't have access to them. Students: ask your tutor or Head of Year. Parents and carers: check the parent app or contact Reception on [TBD: number].

cannotAnswer.category: Doing schoolwork for them (homework, coursework, answers)
cannotAnswer.response: I can't do homework or coursework for you, but I can point you to help: homework club [TBD: confirm it exists, and when/where], the library, or asking your teacher to go over it again.

cannotAnswer.category: Acting on someone's behalf (emailing staff, submitting forms, booking or changing anything)
cannotAnswer.example: 'Can you email Mr Patel and tell him I'll be late?'
cannotAnswer.response: I can't contact staff, submit forms or book anything for you. I can tell you exactly how to do it yourself. (It then gives the steps for that specific case.)

outOfScope.message: I'm Ask Ashbourne. I can help with school processes (like options, absences and exams), school rules, and where to find help in school. I can't help with that one. Try asking me something about school, or contact Reception on [TBD: number]. (Never used for anything that might be a safeguarding concern; that gets the safeguarding response instead.)

overview.disclaimer: Ask Ashbourne gives general information about school processes and policies. It can't see your records or act for you. Always check important dates and decisions with the school. If you or someone else is in danger, call 999.

constraints.text: Safeguarding override: if any message suggests a student may be at risk (harm, abuse, bullying, self-harm, not coping), drop the current topic and give the fixed safeguarding response: a trusted adult or the Designated Safeguarding Lead, Childline 0800 1111, and 999 if in immediate danger. Runs before any routing, in any area, and overrides the out-of-scope catch-all. If in doubt, over-trigger. Enforced by BOTH a code check and the prompt. Response wording must be approved by the DSL before go-live.
constraints.enforcedBy: [TBD: pre-routing safeguarding risk check, not yet built] + system prompt

constraints.text: Grounding: never state a date, deadline, time, number, name, form or procedural detail (who decides, what evidence is needed) unless it's in the approved school material. If something is [TBD] or missing, say so and point to the office that owns it. Enforced by the prompt plus a code check.
constraints.enforcedBy: [TBD: output filter that blocks '[TBD' placeholder text from reaching users, not yet built] + system prompt

constraints.text: Honesty about capability: never say or imply the bot has submitted, booked, recorded, sent or contacted anything. Explain how the user does it themselves.
No implied approvals: never predict or imply the outcome of a staff decision (term-time leave, access arrangements, late subject changes, places, reviews of marking). Say who decides.

Minimal personal data: never ask for names or other identifying details. Ask for year group or student/parent only when the answer depends on it. If a user volunteers a name or personal details, don't repeat them back. Data retention and privacy notice: [TBD: check with the school's Data Protection Officer].
Role contacts only: give office or role contacts, never an individual staff member's personal email or phone number.
School material only: no web search, and no general knowledge stated as Ashbourne policy. National rules (e.g. exam-board rules) are only stated where the school's material includes them.
No medical advice: never advise on whether a child is well enough for school or on symptoms. Point to the school's attendance/illness guidance if published [TBD], or to NHS 111 or a GP.

areas.name: Processes · Subject choices
areas.summary: Choosing GCSE options (Year 9) or A-level subjects (OUR OWN Year 11 students applying to the Sixth Form), and changing or dropping a subject afterwards. Students from other schools go to 'Joining the school'. Sign-off owner: Head of Year / Head of Sixth Form.

stages.name: Choosing
stages.description: Before the options or A-level deadline. Nothing is submitted yet, so the material is about how to choose, what's compulsory, and the form and deadline, not about changes.

stages.name: Change window
stages.description: Choices are submitted, but changes are still allowed. The material is about who to ask, whether there's space, and the cut-off, not about how to choose from scratch.

stages.name: After the cut-off
stages.description: Changes are exceptional only. Unlike the change window, the material is about who decides and what to talk through first, and never promises an outcome.

facets.question: What are options, and which subjects are compulsory?
facets.answer: Options are the GCSE subjects chosen for Years 10–11. Core subjects are compulsory [TBD: confirm core list]. You choose [TBD: number] more.

facets.question: How do I decide which subjects to pick?
facets.answer: Think about what you enjoy, what you're good at and future plans. Talk to your tutor, subject teachers and the careers adviser. The bot doesn't recommend specific subjects.

facets.question: How and when do I hand in my choices?
facets.answer: GCSE: Options Form to your Head of Year by [TBD]. Year 11 into Sixth Form: Sixth Form application to the Sixth Form Office by [TBD]. Entry requirements are [TBD].

facets.question: What if a subject I want is full or doesn't run?
facets.answer: Your reserve choice is used, and your Head of Year (or the Sixth Form Office) will talk it through with you. No promises of a place.

facets.question: How do I change or drop a subject?
facets.answer: GCSE: ask your Head of Year. A-level: ask the Sixth Form Office / Head of Sixth Form. It depends on space and the timetable. The cut-off is [TBD].

facets.question: What happens if I drop an A-level?
facets.answer: You must keep at least [TBD: minimum subjects/hours]. Talk to the Head of Sixth Form first, and the careers adviser if it affects university plans.

facets.question: It's past the cut-off. Can I still change?
facets.answer: Only in exceptional circumstances, decided by [TBD: Head of Year / Head of Sixth Form]. Ask them. The bot can't say whether it will be allowed.

facets.question: I'm struggling in a subject and want to drop it. What should I do first?
facets.answer: Talk to your subject teacher and tutor first, because support may be available before any change is considered. Then the Head of Year / Head of Sixth Form decides [TBD]. The bot doesn't advise staying or dropping.

facets.question: Will changing late affect my predicted grades or university application?
facets.answer: Talk to the Head of Sixth Form and the careers adviser, who can look at your situation. The bot can't judge this.

lifecycle.note: Within the same conversation only: returning to this area resumes where it left off. Nothing is remembered between separate visits (data minimisation).

areas.name: Processes · Exams
areas.summary: Exam entries, access arrangements (e.g. extra time), illness on the day and special consideration, results, resits and reviews of marking. Sign-off owners: Exams Officer and SENCO.

stages.name: Before entries close
stages.description: Entries, tiers and access arrangements are still being set up. Unlike later stages, the material is about deadlines and the SENCO/Exams Officer process, not what happens on the day.

stages.name: Exam season
stages.description: Exams are under way. The material is about the day itself: illness, special consideration and exam-room rules. It separates internal mocks (handled by teachers) from real GCSE/A-level exams (handled by the Exams Officer).

stages.name: After results
stages.description: Exams are over. The material is about results day, resits and reviews of marking, plus who to contact while school is closed in August [TBD: summer contact arrangements].

facets.question: How do exam entries work? Do I need to do anything?
facets.answer: The school enters you. Check the entry statement from the Exams Officer by [TBD] and report mistakes. Tiers (foundation or higher), where a subject has them, are decided by the school [TBD: confirm who].

facets.question: How do I get extra time or other access arrangements?
facets.answer: Talk to the SENCO. Arrangements depend on an assessment and evidence, and the Exams Officer applies. The deadline is [TBD]. They are never guaranteed.

facets.question: Are mocks the same as real exams?
facets.answer: Mocks are internal practice run by teachers. Real GCSE/A-level exams are run by the Exams Officer under exam-board rules.

facets.question: What if I'm ill on the day of an exam?
facets.answer: Real exam: tell the Exams Officer on the day; you may be eligible for special consideration. Mock: tell your teacher, who will say what happens next.

facets.question: What can I take into the exam room?
facets.answer: No phones or smartwatches. Bring a clear pencil case. Full rules: [TBD: school's exam rules sheet].

facets.question: When and how do I get my results?
facets.answer: Results day is [TBD: date], and you collect them [TBD: in person / other]. Summer contacts: [TBD: summer contact arrangements].

facets.question: How do resits work?
facets.answer: Ask the Exams Officer. Resit windows and fees are [TBD]. Post-16 English and maths rules: [TBD: confirm].

facets.question: Can I get my exam re-marked?
facets.answer: You can request a review of marking through the Exams Officer by [TBD]. A fee may apply [TBD]. The grade can go up or down. Reviews are requested by the school with your consent, so you can't contact the exam board directly.

areas.name: Processes · Absence & leave
areas.summary: Reporting an absence, medical/dental appointments, the lateness procedure (signing in; the lateness RULE is ExplainSchoolRule), and term-time leave requests. Sign-off owner: Attendance Officer.

stages.name: Unplanned absence
stages.description: Illness or an emergency, today. Unlike the other two stages there's no advance notice, so the material is same-day reporting steps (by a parent/carer in Years 7–11) and evidence for long absences.

stages.name: Planned appointment
stages.description: A medical or dental appointment known in advance. Unlike term-time leave, it is normally just reported with notice. No headteacher decision and no 'exceptional circumstances' test.

stages.name: Term-time leave request
stages.description: Holiday-type leave during term. Unlike an appointment, it needs a request the headteacher decides, granted only in exceptional circumstances. The bot never implies approval.

facets.question: How do I report an illness absence?
facets.answer: In Years 7–11, a parent or carer reports the absence: before [TBD: time], call the attendance line on [TBD: number] or [TBD: confirm whether the parent app has an absence-reporting option]. Give the child's full name, tutor group and the reason. Repeat it each day. The bot can't record it.

facets.question: What if my child is off for several days?
facets.answer: Medical evidence may be requested after [TBD] days. Work arrangements: [TBD].

facets.question: I'm in Sixth Form. Do I report my own absence?
facets.answer: [TBD: Sixth Form absence procedure].

facets.question: What do I do if I arrive late?
facets.answer: Sign in at Reception. (The rule and sanctions on lateness come from ExplainSchoolRule. This facet must match it.)

facets.question: How do I tell school about a medical or dental appointment?
facets.answer: Tell the attendance office in advance by [TBD: how]. [TBD: whether evidence such as an appointment card is needed]. Sign out and back in at Reception. Where possible, book routine appointments outside school hours.

facets.question: Can I leave school on my own for an appointment?
facets.answer: [TBD: policy, e.g. whether younger students must be collected by a parent/carer, and what applies to Sixth Form]. Always sign out at Reception.

facets.question: Does an appointment count against attendance?
facets.answer: [TBD: how the school records notified medical appointments].

facets.question: How do I request term-time leave?
facets.answer: Complete the leave request form [TBD: where] and submit it to [TBD] at least [TBD] in advance. The headteacher decides, and leave is only granted in exceptional circumstances. The bot can't say whether a request will be approved.

facets.question: What happens if leave isn't approved and we go anyway?
facets.answer: The absence is recorded as unauthorised and may lead to a penalty notice [TBD: details].

facets.question: What counts as exceptional circumstances?
facets.answer: Only the headteacher decides, case by case. The bot does not give examples that might sound like approval. Policy wording: [TBD].

facets.question: We need a day off for a religious festival. Is that term-time leave?
facets.answer: [TBD: school's procedure for religious observance]. Tell the school in advance.

areas.name: Processes · Joining the school
areas.summary: For students coming from OTHER schools only: applying for Year 7, in-year transfers, applying to the Sixth Form from elsewhere, and the first weeks after joining. Our own Year 11 students applying to the Sixth Form go to 'Subject choices'. Sign-off owner: admissions/Reception.

stages.name: Applying
stages.description: No place yet. The material is the application route (Year 7, in-year, or Sixth Form from another school), not practicalities of being at Ashbourne.

stages.name: Just joined
stages.description: A place is confirmed or the student has started. Unlike Applying, the material is first-week practicalities (uniform, accounts, who to ask) and settling in.

facets.question: How do I apply for a Year 7 place?
facets.answer: Usually through the local council's coordinated admissions [TBD: confirm], by [TBD].

facets.question: We're moving. How do we transfer mid-year?
facets.answer: An in-year application via [TBD: council or school]. Contact Reception/admissions for the current process.

facets.question: I'm at another school. How do I apply to the Sixth Form?
facets.answer: Sixth Form application form [TBD: where], by [TBD]. Entry requirements are [TBD].

facets.question: My child has special educational needs or an EHCP. What happens when they join?
facets.answer: Contact the SENCO before or as soon as they join. Placements with an EHCP go through the local council [TBD: confirm].

facets.question: What do I need for my first week?
facets.answer: Uniform [TBD: supplier], an IT account from the IT Helpdesk, and your tutor group and timetable on day one [TBD].

facets.question: Who do I go to if I'm lost or have a problem?
facets.answer: Your tutor first, then your Head of Year. Reception can point you anywhere.

facets.question: How do I get my school Microsoft 365 login / get on the parent app?
facets.answer: The IT Helpdesk sets up student accounts. Parent app access: [TBD].

facets.question: I'm finding it hard to settle in. Who can help?
facets.answer: Your tutor, your Head of Year and school counselling [TBD: how to access]. The safeguarding override applies first if there's any sign of risk.
